body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and all sufficiently large \(n\), there is \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\Phi_{j,n}\) such that
\[
 \max_{t\in\Gamma_n}|\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)-\phi_j(t)|\le \tau_{e,n}.
\]
For \(j=2\), its representing atomic law also satisfies
\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}\right|
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and \(n\).  Define
\[
 U_j^H=\max\{-H_n,\min\{U_j,H_n\}\}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}moment}\) and \(\mathbf 1\{|U_j|>H_n\}\le |U_j|^{q_e}H_n^{-q_e}\) give
\[
 P(|U_j|>H_n)\le M_eH_n^{-q_e}.
\]
Consequently, for every real \(t\),
\[
 \left|E_Pe^{itU_j^H}-\phi_j(t)\right|
 \le2P(|U_j|>H_n)
 \le2M_eH_n^{-q_e}=\tau_{e,n},                                    \tag{1}
\]
and clipping gives
\[
 E_P|U_j^H|^{q_e}\le E_P|U_j|^{q_e}\le M_e.                       \tag{2}
\]
For \(j=2\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\), \(q_e>1\), and \(|u|\mathbf 1\{|u|>H_n\}\le |u|^{q_e}H_n^{1-q_e}\) give
\[
 |E_PU_2^H|
 =|E_P(U_2^H-U_2)|
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.                                               \tag{3}
\]

Put \(D=2|\Gamma_n|+2\), and define the continuous map
\[
 v(u)=\bigl((\operatorname{Re}e^{itu},\operatorname{Im}e^{itu})_{t\in\Gamma_n},u,|u|^{q_e}\bigr)
 \in\mathbb R^D.
\]
The vector \(E_Pv(U_j^H)\) lies in the convex hull of the compact set \(v([-H_n,H_n])\): finite simple-function approximations to the integral lie in that convex hull, and a convex hull of a compact subset of a finite-dimensional space is compact.

We give the finite-support reduction explicitly.  If a convex representation uses more than \(D+1\) points, the augmented vectors \((1,v(u_r))\in\mathbb R^{D+1}\) are linearly dependent.  Thus coefficients \(a_r\), not all zero, satisfy \(\sum_ra_r=0\) and \(\sum_ra_rv(u_r)=0\).  After changing the common sign if necessary, some \(a_r>0\).  Subtracting \(c(a_r)_r\) from the weights, where \(c=\min_{a_r>0}w_r/a_r\), preserves their sum and barycenter, keeps all weights nonnegative, and makes at least one weight zero.  Iteration leaves at most
\[
 D+1=2|\Gamma_n|+3\le M_n
\]
atoms.  Padding with zero-weight atoms at \(H_n\) and ordering the locations produces an atomic characteristic function \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\) that agrees with \(E_Pe^{itU_j^H}\) at every \(t\in\Gamma_n\), has the same mean and \(q_e\)-moment, and is supported on \([-H_n,H_n]\).  Equations (1)--(3) yield
\[
 \max_{t\in\Gamma_n}|\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)-\phi_j(t)|\le\tau_{e,n}, \tag{4}
\]
and, for \(j=2\),
\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}\right|
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.                                               \tag{5}
\]

It remains only to check the explicit protected-neighborhood constraint in the corrected \(\mathrm{def{:}error\text{-}sieves}\).  By (2), the atomic law satisfies \(\sum_\ell w_{j\ell}|u_{j\ell}|^{q_e}\le M_e\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}derived\text{-}protected\text{-}neighborhood}\) to this atomic law gives directly
\[
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_*}|\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)|\ge c_*.                    \tag{6}
\]
Thus the support, probability-weight, moment, and protected-frequency restrictions of \(\widetilde\Phi_{j,n}\) all hold.  For \(j=2\), (5) is stronger than the additional bound \(2M_eH_n^{1-q_e}\) defining \(\Phi_{2,n}\).  Hence \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\Phi_{j,n}\), and (4)--(5) prove the result.  The threshold \(q_e>1\) is used exactly in (3), where it makes the centering error vanish as \(H_n\to\infty\); no separately assumed spectral modulus is used.
